The claim states that Hard Pruning is a density control method in 3D Gaussian Splatting that reduces model size by a constant ratio at fixed intervals after the densification stage. Source [S1] explicitly confirms that Hard Pruning 'prunes the model by a constant ratio every 3000 iterations starting at iteration 15000' and notes that these iterations occur 'after the densification stage.' Source [S2] corroborates that Hard Pruning is 'performed after the densification stage' and serves to reduce the number of Gaussians (density control). All specific details in the claim are present in the provided evidence.

Hard Pruning was introduced in Speedy-Splat as part of a sparse primitive strategy for fast 3D Gaussian Splatting [S1, S2].

The claim states that Hard Pruning was introduced in Speedy-Splat as part of a sparse primitive strategy for fast 3D Gaussian Splatting. Source [S1] explicitly describes 'Hard Pruning' as a method that prunes Gaussians after the densification stage (a sparse primitive strategy) to refine the model, noting it reduces the number of Gaussians by 10.6x (implying speed/efficiency gains). Source [S2] confirms that Hard Pruning is performed after the densification stage and, together with Soft Pruning, reduces the number of Gaussians by approximately 90%, increasing rendering and training speed. Both sources align with the description of Hard Pruning being a post-densification pruning method used to optimize (make faster/sparser) 3D Gaussian Splatting models.
